basic_identification.name: Manifold
basic_identification.originator: Eric Diep, Richerd Chan, Wilkins Chung (Manifold.xyz)

core_ideas.core_claim: Creators should own their smart contracts. Manifold enables artists to deploy their own ERC-721/ERC-1155 contracts, retaining full provenance, royalty control, and portability across all marketplaces. The creator is the platform.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Digitally native in that it leverages blockchain smart contracts as the substrate for art distribution. The contract itself becomes the artist's identity layer on-chain -- not just a wrapper for images but an extensible programmable canvas for custom minting mechanics, burn-redeem logic, and dynamic NFTs.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: Manifold is infrastructure-level and largely attention-neutral. It does not run a marketplace feed or algorithmic discovery. Artists must bring their own audience. However, its bridge to OpenSea, Rarible, and other attention-driven marketplaces means art minted via Manifold ultimately circulates within attention-economy platforms. Manifold itself does not optimize for engagement but enables participation in systems that do.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Strongly intention-native. Manifold addresses a declared structural need: artist sovereignty over contracts and provenance. It does not capture engagement or extract platform rent from creators. Its design philosophy is infrastructure-first, serving the artist's need for ownership rather than the platform's need for traffic.

market_economics.revenue_model: Free for creators. Small per-piece fee charged to buyers (not percentage-based). Seed funding of $7.9M (2021) from a16z, Christie's Ventures, Initialized Capital. Revenue also from partnership arrangements with high-profile users. Annual on-chain revenue approximately $84K (DeFi Llama, 2025), indicating significant post-crash contraction.
market_economics.market_position: Infrastructure layer. Manifold sits beneath marketplaces -- it is the contract deployment and minting layer that feeds into primary and secondary markets (OpenSea, Rarible, Foundation, SuperRare, Zora).
market_economics.price_range: N/A -- Manifold is not a marketplace. Art minted via Manifold ranges from free claims to six-figure sales depending on the artist and marketplace.
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Declining from 2021-2022 peaks. On-chain revenue dropped significantly post-crash. However, Manifold remains the de facto standard for serious NFT creators. Volume reflects broader NFT market contraction rather than platform-specific failure. The platform highlighted '230 Notable NFTs of 2025' suggesting continued cultural relevance despite lower volume.
market_economics.collector_demographics: Primarily crypto-native collectors. Some crossover with traditional art world through high-profile users (Jay-Z, Steve Aoki, Sotheby's partnerships). Institutional interest via Christie's Ventures investment. Skews toward technically literate collectors who understand contract provenance.
market_economics.sustainability: Uncertain. The free-for-creators model depends on sufficient minting volume for buyer fees to sustain operations, plus venture runway. At ~$84K annual revenue, the platform likely operates at a loss. Sustainability depends on either NFT market recovery or evolution of the business model. The structural value (artist-owned contracts, royalty registry) provides durable utility even at low volume.

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: Manifold Studio (no-code web interface), Solidity smart contracts (ERC-721, ERC-1155), Extensions framework for custom logic, Manifold Bridge for marketplace interoperability. Compatible with IPFS, Arweave for media storage. Developer SDK available for custom integrations.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: Largely irrelevant to Manifold's core function. AI-generated art can be minted via Manifold like any other digital artwork. The platform is medium-agnostic -- it concerns itself with contract infrastructure, not the production process. Some AI artists use Manifold to deploy their collections.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Static artifact at the contract level, though the extensions framework supports dynamic NFTs that can evolve, respond to events, or change state. The contract itself is immutable once deployed.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Manifold contributes infrastructure vocabulary rather than aesthetic vocabulary: creator contract, contract provenance, extensions, burn-redeem, on-chain royalties. It has shifted how artists and collectors talk about ownership and authenticity but does not define visual or conceptual aesthetics.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Strongly openness-leaning: open-source contract code, interoperable with all marketplaces. Commons-contributing through the Royalty Registry (adopted across the ecosystem). Infrastructure over spectacle. Individual sovereignty (artist-owned contracts) rather than collective governance.

infrastructure_governance.openness: Partially open-source. The Manifold Creator contract source code is provided by Manifold but deployed by the artist. The Royalty Registry is open and adopted ecosystem-wide. The Extensions framework is open for third-party development. Manifold Studio itself is proprietary.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: Founding-team governed. No DAO, no community governance. Decisions about platform development, features, and direction are made by the Manifold team. However, because artists own their contracts, they retain sovereignty over their own on-chain presence regardless of Manifold's decisions.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: Strong artist sovereignty. Artists own and control their smart contracts independently of Manifold. If Manifold disappears, the contracts persist on Ethereum. Metadata and media storage depend on the chosen solution (IPFS, Arweave, etc.). Artists can set their own royalty structures. The contract is signed by the artist's wallet, not Manifold's.
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: Excellent. Built on ERC-721/1155 standards. Manifold Bridge connects to all major marketplaces. The Royalty Registry has been adopted by all major marketplaces as a single source of truth. API available for developers. Contracts are fully portable.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: Smart contracts are permanent on Ethereum. Media preservation depends on artist's choice -- IPFS, Arweave, or centralized hosting. Manifold encourages but does not enforce decentralized storage. The contract and on-chain metadata persist as long as Ethereum operates.
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: Binary: artists choose to deploy contracts and mint. No granular consent for how minted works are displayed across marketplaces. Burn-redeem mechanics offer some consent-like control (holders must actively opt in to transformations). No machine-readable consent standards.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Integration through high-profile partnerships (Christie's Ventures investor, Sotheby's auction partnerships, major artists). Manifold bridges the crypto-native and traditional art worlds by providing institutional-grade contract infrastructure that traditional players can trust.
field_position.what_it_enables: Artists can deploy their own smart contracts without coding, retaining provenance, royalty control, and brand identity across all marketplaces. Custom minting mechanics (burn-redeem, claim pages, dynamic NFTs). A royalty standard adopted ecosystem-wide.
field_position.what_it_lacks: No built-in discovery or curation. No preservation guarantees for media assets. No community governance or collective decision-making. No support for non-Ethereum chains (recently added Base but primarily Ethereum-centric). No structured metadata standards beyond basic NFT metadata. No interoperability with non-blockchain art systems.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Artists without crypto wallet literacy. Those who cannot afford Ethereum gas fees (though L2 support helps). Artists working outside the NFT paradigm. Those in regions with restricted crypto access. The technical barrier, while reduced by no-code tools, still requires understanding of blockchain concepts.
field_position.frontier_signal: Established infrastructure. Not frontier in itself but enables frontier practices. The extensions framework pushes toward programmable art but Manifold's core value proposition (artist-owned contracts) is now standard rather than novel.

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: None built-in. Discovery happens through marketplaces (OpenSea, etc.), social media (Twitter/X), and artist communities. Manifold provides the infrastructure but not the attention surface.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: Low platform-level dependency. Manifold would survive if Twitter/Instagram disappeared because its value is in contract infrastructure, not social reach. However, artists using Manifold depend heavily on social media for distribution.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Strongly intention-native. Addresses the declared structural need for artist ownership and contract portability. Does not capture engagement or extract attention rent. The Royalty Registry serves a field-wide infrastructure need.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Significant. The Royalty Registry is a public good adopted across the NFT ecosystem. Open-source contract templates. The artist-owned contract model has become the expected standard, shifting norms from platform-controlled to creator-controlled infrastructure.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Ownership primarily. Contract provenance (who deployed, when, verified source code) plus ownership chain on-chain. Does not track meaning, exhibition history, or critical reception.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Archival. On-chain records are permanent and timestamped. No cyclical, anticipatory, or real-time temporal features beyond block timestamps.
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: Does not address absence. Tracks only what is present on-chain. No mechanism for representing what is missing from the field or gaps in provenance.

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Neither explicitly. Manifold provides infrastructure that supports multiple approaches without enforcing a single truth or cultivating coherence across uses. Each artist's contract is sovereign.
coherence.contestability: Limited. Contract terms are set by the artist and enforced by code. Once deployed, the contract is immutable. Royalty rates, minting rules, and transfer mechanics cannot be contested by collectors -- they are take-it-or-leave-it. The Extensions framework allows some evolution but the base contract is fixed.
coherence.forkability: Moderately forkable. The contract source code is available, so others could deploy similar infrastructure. However, the network effects (Royalty Registry adoption, marketplace integration) are hard to replicate. Individual artist contracts are fully sovereign and do not depend on Manifold continuing to exist.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The principle that creators own their infrastructure. Manifold's model of deploying sovereignty to the individual rather than aggregating control is directly relevant to A(DAI)'s commons architecture. The Royalty Registry as a public good standard adopted ecosystem-wide is a model for how A(DAI) could establish shared vocabulary or metadata standards. The Extensions framework shows how to make infrastructure extensible without losing coherence.
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: Manifold's limitation to ownership provenance only. A(DAI) needs provenance of meaning, not just ownership chains. Also refuse the single-chain dependency (Ethereum-centric) and the lack of structured metadata beyond basic NFT fields. Refuse the absence of community governance -- Manifold is founder-controlled infrastructure, while A(DAI) should be commons-governed.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: Manifold proves that artist sovereignty is viable at the infrastructure level, but its sovereignty is individual not collective. A(DAI) must solve the harder problem: how to build collective intelligence infrastructure that preserves individual sovereignty. Manifold shows the contract-as-identity pattern works, but A(DAI) needs identity to be relational, not isolated.

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: Subject to evolving NFT and crypto regulations. Royalty enforcement is increasingly voluntary across marketplaces, undermining a core value proposition. No direct EU AI Act exposure. Copyright questions around NFTs apply to art minted via Manifold but are not Manifold-specific. Smart contract code is verifiable on-chain, providing transparency.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: Mixed. Manifold's contract code is provided as-is. IP of minted works belongs entirely to the artist. Each artist sets their own license terms. No platform-level IP claims on creator work. The Royalty Registry is an open standard.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Opt-in. Artists actively choose to deploy contracts and set terms. Collectors actively choose to mint. No opt-out regime -- participation is entirely voluntary.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Ethereum blockchain (and recently Base L2). Depends on marketplace ecosystem for distribution (OpenSea, etc.). Contract infrastructure is independent -- if Manifold Studio disappears, deployed contracts persist. Media storage depends on IPFS/Arweave infrastructure.
ecosystem.network_effects: Hub for creator contract deployment. The Royalty Registry creates network effects as a shared standard. However, Manifold itself is not a network -- it is tooling. Its network effects are indirect, operating through the contracts it enables across the ecosystem.
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Surviving but contracted. Revenue dropped to ~$84K annually from likely much higher 2021-2022 levels. Team reduced to ~15 people. Still recognized as the standard for serious NFT creators. Pivoting toward Base L2 and lower-cost minting. Cultural relevance maintained through curation of notable NFTs and continued tool development.
